title: Omitting the owner pronoun with one thing
summary: Leave out meidän or teidän while keeping the noun ending; retain heidän with singular possessed nouns.
targetSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
objectives: Leave out meidän or teidän while keeping the noun ending; retain heidän with singular possessed nouns.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: Keep the ending when omitting the pronoun
paragraphs: Leave out meidän or teidän while keeping the noun ending; retain heidän with singular possessed nouns.
Tämä on meidän pallomme. and Tämä on pallomme. mean the same thing: “This is our ball”.
In these identification sentences retain heidän: its third-person ending does not identify the intended owner by itself. Omission in other sentence structures is outside this lesson.
Follow an explicit request to omit or retain the owner pronoun. Otherwise both ordinary first- and second-person forms are accepted.

steps: Tämä on (“This is”) identifies one thing.
The ending identifies the owner, so omit meidän while retaining the noun ending.
Tämä on (“This is”) identifies one thing.
The ending identifies the owner, so omit teidän while retaining the noun ending.
Tämä on (“This is”) identifies one thing.
Retain heidän in this identification pattern so the owner stays clear.

commonMistakes: Omitting the owner pronoun does not remove its noun ending.
Retain heidän in this bounded identification pattern.
